solution: Call a position a barrier when a[i] <= m. A subarray has minimum exactly m with a single copy of m iff it contains exactly one barrier and that barrier holds the value m. Since all entries are positive, the best such subarray around a given m-barrier is the maximal one: it runs from just after the previous barrier to just before the next. So scan the barrier list once and, for every barrier whose value is m, take the prefix-sum of the open span between its neighbours, keeping the maximum. O(n) time and O(n) space per dataset, n <= 10^5.
statement_summary: Given an array of positive integers and a value m, the task is the largest sum of a contiguous subarray whose minimum element equals m and which contains exactly one copy of m. The array holds up to 10^5 entries, each at most 64, and always contains at least one entry equal to m; several datasets follow.
notes: O(n^2) brute force over every subarray agrees on 3000 random arrays plus the sample (12). The positivity of the entries is what makes maximal extension optimal; with zeros or negatives this reduction would fail.
